harness_signal: make:module is listed in `guren --help` and, in the shipped condition, in the harness entry file (make:module plus --module on every make:*); `guren context` does not mention modules. make:module writes the module skeleton, the root db/schema.ts re-export and the createApp({ modules }) entry in one step. guren check reports the module's schema aggregation ('db/schema.ts re-exports modules/newsletter/db/schema.ts') and runs the zero-config module boundary rule, which fails top-level code importing a module's internals (so routes registered from routes/web.ts with the module's controller go red) but allows imports of a module's index.ts and db/schema.ts, which is why the ticket's blog-to-module ban needs a declared guren.arch.ts rule. The arch file is findable only through `guren check --help` (--arch: 'architecture boundary checks (guren.arch.ts)'), the @guren/cli README's subpath table (@guren/cli/arch: defineArchRules()) and its dist types; no shipped harness file mentions it. guren audit warns (never fails) that the two public POST routes have no authentication check, and warns about a token column serialized without `hidden`. Plain guren check's exit code is informational, so the hidden test asserts on its parsed --json failures. Traps and framework gaps: the arch checker's resolver tries the raw path first and accepts a directory, so a directory import ('../modules/newsletter', the exact extensionless spelling make:module writes into src/app.ts) resolves to 'modules/newsletter', matches no 'modules/newsletter/**' glob and escapes both the declared rule and the module boundary rule with no warning (the hidden static import scan still catches it); a table declared in the root schema instead of the module schema passes guren check with only a warning that db/schema.ts no longer re-exports the module schema; Controller has no redirect-back helper, so the Referer is read by hand (echoing it raw is an open redirect).
